lesson.subject: literacy
lesson.title: Voice Power
lesson.subtitle: Term 4 Week 7, Session 2
lesson.footer: Persuasive Speeches | Year 5/6 Literacy | Week 7 Session 2

plan.curriculum: English 2.0, Level 5: VC2E5LY02 delivering spoken texts using features of voice (pace, pause, volume, emphasis); VC2E5LY06 reading aloud fluently for meaning
plan.shape: warm up, model a marked script, practise, perform: a voice warm-up game, a modelled mark-up code, practice marking lines, then pairs mark up and perform their own speech lines
plan.criticalFeature: the pause before the key word makes the audience listen; stress only the word that matters most
decisionPoints: the choice check: the mark-up that makes the key word land
the exit board: a new line marked up
plan.anchor: Claim it. Prove it. Sell it. Say it. Today: say it with your voice.
plan.catchUp: Missed Week 6? The mark-up code is taught from scratch; use any persuasive paragraph from your writing book.

studentTools: Speech lines written in Week 6 (opening, story, vision)
routineIcons: Write it, chin it, show me
Point to A, B or C
boardSetup: Mark-up code: / short pause, // long pause, CAPS = stress the word, (slow) (fast)

resources.label: Worksheet
resources.description: Your turn: read mark-up, fix a misplaced pause, mark up lines, then mark up your own speech.
resources.title: Voice Power
resources.subtitle: Pause before it. Stress the one word that matters.

example.answer: Read normally, wait two seconds, then say ONE with weight.

items.prompt: What does the speaker do at each mark?
rows: Ice to hunt / ice to live.
And then // the ice was gone.
answers: Ice to hunt / ice to live.
a short pause between the two
And then // the ice was gone.
a long pause before the ice was gone

example.prompt: Where should the pause go? The bears are / starving.
steps: Put the pause just before it

items.prompt: Which mark-up makes the key word land?
options: Please / switch off one light tonight.
Please switch off one light // TONIGHT.
Please switch // off one light tonight.
items.explain: The long pause and stress land on tonight, the word that matters.

items.prompt: Leo marked up his line. Find the problem and fix it.
work: WE MUST SAVE OUR CREEK FROM RUBBISH.
items.answer: Stressing every word means nothing stands out. Fix: We must save our creek // from RUBBISH.

example.prompt: Plain: We can still save the reef.
example.answer: We can still // SAVE the reef.

items.prompt: Mark up each line with / // and CAPS.
rows: One bag can trap one turtle.
They waited and the ice never came.
This is our school and our choice.
answers: One bag can trap // one turtle.
One bag can trap // ONE turtle.
They waited and the ice never came.
They waited / and waited // the ice never CAME.
This is our school and our choice.
This is OUR school / and OUR choice.

steps: Copy four lines of your speech
example.answer: I dream of bears / with room to ROAM.

items.prompt: Copy four lines from your speech and mark them up. Then rehearse them aloud with a partner.
items.answer: Four marked lines: pauses before key words and one stressed word per line.

resources.label: Extension
resources.description: Early finisher option: direct a line three ways, then write director's notes for your speech.
resources.title: Voice Director
resources.subtitle: Directors tell actors exactly how to say each line.

example.answer: Hopeful: It's NOT too late! Urgent: It's not too late // YET. Quiet: (slow) It's... not... too late.

items.prompt: Mark up each line three different ways.
answers: The bears are waiting / for US.

steps: Pick your three most important lines
example.answer: Line 1: slow and quiet, so they lean in.

items.prompt: Write director's notes for the three most important lines of your speech: how to say each one, and why.
items.answer: Three lines with voice choices and reasons linked to the audience.

resources.label: Supported Worksheet
resources.description: Supported option: picture-clue choices, a first line marked and a frame.
resources.title: Voice Helper
resources.subtitle: / means pause. CAPS means say it strongly.

items.hint: The slash means stop for a moment.
The first one is done for you.

items.prompt: Copy one line from your speech. Mark it up. Say it to your partner.
items.answer: A marked line with a pause and one stressed word.

slides.notes: Open the session. One line: the same words can fall flat or bring the house down. Today we learn why.

No video today. Print the Worksheet for everyone, the Extension for early finishers and the Supported Worksheet for those who need it. Write the mark-up code on the board. Students need their Week 6 speech lines.

slides.learningIntention: We are learning to use our voice to make a speech powerful.
successCriteria: I can read a script marked for pauses and stress.
I can mark up a speech so the key words land.
I can perform my lines with pace, pause and emphasis.

beats: POINT to the learning intention.
SAY: Great words need a great voice. Today you find yours.
SAY: Read the I can lines with me. Everyone, together, on three.
SAY: The first one is where we all start.
The second one is today's main goal.
notes.prep: SC1 is reachable for all; SC2 is the core and the exit evidence; SC3 is the stretch.

slides.title: Same line, five ways
lines: Say it: excited, bored, whispering, like a robot, like a coach.

notes.answer: open - the same words sound completely different
beats: SAY: One line. Five voices. Let's warm up.
Everyone stand.
ASK: Say it excited... now bored... now whispering... robot... coach!
3 sec each. Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
EXPECT: five very different versions
ASK: Which voice would actually convince the principal?
15 sec. Turn and tell, partner A first.
EXPECT: the coach; calm and confident
SAY: Your voice can make or break your words. Sit down.
trap: Fix: say one more round, then freeze; make the last one serious.
notes.prep: Movement and voice warm-up; low-coupling, everyone can join. 3 minutes.

slides.meaning: Saying one word with extra force so it stands out.

notes.answer: saying one word with extra force so it stands out
beats: POINT to the word. SAY: Emphasis. Say it with me. Emphasis.
SAY: Saying one word with extra force so it stands out.
SAY: We must act NOW.
ASK: Say We must act now, stressing a different word each time.
10 sec. Turn and tell, partner B first.
EXPECT: the meaning shifts with the stressed word
trap: Fix: say if everything is loud, nothing stands out. One word per line.

rows: Ice to hunt / ice to live.

notes.answer: / short pause, // long pause, CAPS stress, (slow) (fast) pace
beats: POINT to //.
SAY: And then... (wait two seconds)... it was gone. Feel how you leaned in?
POINT to CAPS.
SAY: We must act NOW. One word. Not every word.
POINT to (slow).
SAY: (slow) Every. Single. Day. Slow makes it heavy.
ASK: Say And then // it was gone with me, with the pause.
3 sec. Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
EXPECT: a real two-second pause
trap: Fix: student counts one-thousand, two-thousand in their head.
notes.stretch: Find where a (fast) section would help your speech.
notes.prep: The model. Critical feature: the pause before the key word makes the audience listen.

slides.title: Stress test
slides.pivot: say the line three ways; which word changes the meaning most?
slides.followUp: cold call one board: say it with your stress

items.text: Only three bins for the whole school.
This may be the last summer the ice lasts.

items.expect: you or today, with a reason

say: Write the ONE word you'd stress in each line.
trap: choosing small words like the or for.
Fix: ask which word carries the meaning? Student re-chooses.
notes.stretch: Explain how the meaning changes if you stress a different word.
notes.help: Look for numbers, you, or the problem word.

slides.title: Where's the pause?
slides.pivot: find the key word first, then put // just before it
slides.followUp: cold call one board: perform it

items.text: The creek used to be full of frogs and now it's silent.
items.answer: The creek used to be full of frogs // and now it's SILENT.

items.text: Three bins for six hundred kids.
items.answer: Three bins // for SIX HUNDRED kids.

items.text: She waited all summer for the ice.
items.answer: She waited / all summer // for the ICE.

say: Copy each line and mark where the pause goes.
trap: a pause after the key word, not before.
Fix: say the pause is the drumroll; it comes first.
notes.stretch: Add CAPS to one word per line.
notes.help: Underline the key word, then put // in front of it.

slides.title: Which mark-up makes the key word land?

options.text: Bring a bottle / to school tomorrow.
options.misconception: the pause is in a place that doesn't matter

options.text: BRING A BOTTLE TO SCHOOL TOMORROW.
options.misconception: stresses everything, so nothing stands out

options.text: Bring a bottle to school // TOMORROW.

notes.answer: C - the pause and stress land on tomorrow
beats: SAY: Three ways to mark the same line.
ASK: Which mark-up makes the key word land?
10 sec. Cue: voices off, everyone points to A, B or C.
EXPECT: pointing to C
SCAN the room, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, cold call: perform C for us.
Less -> perform all three aloud, re-ask.
REVEAL after pointing is scanned.
SAY: C. The pause builds, then tomorrow lands.
trap: pointing to B because it looks loud and strong.
Fix: perform B; ask which word mattered most? Nobody can tell.
notes.prep: Decision point before pairs rehearse. Under 80% means the class marks one line together first.

slides.title: Mark up and rehearse
slides.task: Work through your Worksheet. Finish by marking up four lines of your speech, then rehearse them with a partner.

notes.answer: four marked lines, performed with real pauses
beats: POINT to the task.
SAY: Mark it, then say it. Your partner listens for the pauses.
SAY: Read the task, complete each part, check your work.
Finished? Extension next. Everyone, together, on three.
CIRCULATE. Listen: is there a real pause? Is only one word stressed?
ASK: Perform your four lines to your partner. Partner: thumbs for the best pause.
60 sec each. Turn and tell, partner A first.
EXPECT: real pauses and one stressed word per line
trap: marking pauses but rushing through them when speaking.
Fix: partner taps the desk to count two seconds at each //.
notes.stretch: Extension: direct a line three ways, then write director's notes.
notes.help: Supported Worksheet: picture-clue choices, a first line marked, a frame.
notes.prep: Independent application and paired rehearsal. Toolkit row 8 filled before the exit. SC2 and SC3.

slides.extendedTask: a worksheet ending in four marked-up speech lines, rehearsed aloud

slides.title: Show what you know
questions: Every lunch, our oval fills with wrappers that nobody picks up.
Copy it and mark it up: one // and one CAPS word.

notes.answer: e.g. Every lunch, our oval fills with wrappers // that NOBODY picks up.
beats: SAY: A new line. Mark it so it lands.
ASK: Copy the line and mark it up.
60 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: one // before the key word; one CAPS word
RECORD who marks every word or no key word. Tomorrow's warm-up.
trap: Fix: none now, record the name.
notes.prep: Exit evidence for SC2 on a new line. One board per student.

slides.reflectionPrompt: What will you do with your voice that you didn't do before today?

notes.answer: open - pause before my key word; slow down
beats: SAY: Let's read our I can lines together. Everyone, together, on three.
ASK: How sure are you that you can mark up and perform a speech?
5 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: thumbs up, sideways or down
RECORD each thumb down beside the exit boards.
ASK: What will you do with your
voice that you didn't do before today?
20 sec. Turn and tell, partner B first.
EXPECT: pause before my key word; slow down
notes.prep: Self-assessment read beside the exit boards. Toolkit row 8 filled. SC2.
